Commentary.Commentary: We are back. The players are out. David Warner and Aaron Finch are the openers. Trent Boult to start with the ball. Two slips in place.
...THE CHASE...

Now the home side are under pressure. 200 is a massive score and it won't be easy to chase. Australia do have the firepower and the wicket  tends to get better here. New Zealand on the other hand will back their bowling to defend this. Join us for the chase in a bit.

Finn Allen, one of the stars with the bat is up for an interview. He says he was told last night that he will play. Adds they had a plan and to target the first six overs. Reckons they have got a competitive total and the first half job is done well by them.

Australia just were not up to the mark in the first innings! Their bowlers were way too full earlier on in the search of some swing and paid the price. Later on too, they were guilty of bowling a lot of on-pace deliveries and in the slot when the slower balls were the ones which needed to be bowled. All their bowlers were taken to the cleaners. Hazlewood though was the pick but Australia will not be happy with how they have performed with the ball.

That is a strong batting performance from the visitors and they will be really, really pleased with where they stand in the game at the moment! New Zealand played with intent. Right away Allen was on the attack and put the opposition under massive pressure. They got their fifty up in no time thanks to the right handed opener. He fell and Australia did manage to pull things back but Williamson and Devon Conway kept the score board ticking. They added fifty before Williamson fell. Conway though continued. He was the mainstay and the rest batted alongside him. However, it is Neesham's cameo which could be the difference as his knock took them upto 200.

SIX! A brilliant end to the innings. This is in the slot and Neesham smacks it over wide long on for a biggie. No chance for the fielder there. A six to end the innings. 14 runs off the over and New Zealand reach to the 200-mark.

A run out chance! A better throw was required! On middle, this is hit to long on. Glenn Maxwell there throws it and it's too high for Matthew Wade. He still jumps and has a shy at his end but misses. Two more.

THREE RUNS! Not where Conway intented! A full toss, around off. Conway looks to scoop on the leg side but miscues and it goes off the top edge over short third man. The batters take three runs. Neesham pushes well for the third.
Pitched up, outside off. Neesham lofts it to long off for a single. Devon Conway on the strike.
Two runs! Good running again! New Zealand have been pro active in the middle. Full and on the pads. Neesham helps it to short fine leg. Adam Zampa gets a hand on it and gives away two runs.
Very good from Josh! A yorker, outside off. Neesham fails to dig it out.
FOUR! Starc cannot finish the way he wanted. 10 off this over! This is full and outside off. Conway drives it past cover and it races into the fence. 200 looking possible.
Starc misses his yorker and serves a full toss. Neesham hits it to mid-wicket only for one. Can Mitchell Starc end it nicely?
Very full and on off, worked to long off for a single. Just five of the over so far.

Pitched up on the pads, was the slower one. Conway swings his bat but mistimes it. Marcus Stoinis at deep square leg, runs in and to his left to collect but the ball just bounces in front of him. Well done there by Stoinis. Two more.
Very full and on middle. Neesham looks to heave but gets an inside edge and the ball rolls on the off side. The batters cross. New Zealand are eyeing 200. They need 15 or so runs from this over.
Pitched up, outside off. Conway drives it to extra cover for a single.
In the air but falls safe! On a nagging length, outside off. Neesham swings across but mistimes and the ball flies towards long on and falls in the vacant region.
Good running! Pat Cummins is not happy with the fielder! A full toss. Neesham slams it to long off. Tim David is a bit late to the ball and two runs are taken.
On a length and outside off. Conway knocks through point for a single.
Wide! Pat Cummins changes the angle as he comes 'round the wicket but the issue remains the same. He tires to stay away but bowls way outside off.
This is full and outside off. Neesham drives uppishly but mistimes it to deep cover for a single.
Wide! Angling outside off, and this goes well over the tramline, Neesham swings and misses.
SIX! CLOBBERED! That is why he was send up the order! On a length and outside off, in the arc for Neesham who thumps it across over mid-wicket for a biggie.
Full ball, angling outside off, Devon drives it through covers for a single.
On a length and on leg. Conway nudges it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Short in length and on leg, this is pulled behind square leg for a single.
Length ball, outside off, this is pushed through covers for a single.
Fuller ball, outside off. Neesham tries to smash it away but without any foot movement. The ball goes to long on for a single.
On middle on the shorter side, pulled to deep square leg for a single.

FOUR! Conway on the other side is playing so beautifully. Plays with the field this time. Full and on middle, pitched up. Conway drives it past mid off, and no chance for long on to cut it off as well. Four runs.

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! Josh Hazlewood has been the best bowler of the lot so far and by many miles. Excellent delivery to get rid of Phillips! Josh bangs it hard in the deck, around off and on the shorter side. Glenn Phillips looks to pull but was cramped for the room a bit. He gets a top edge and the ball lobs nicely for Josh Hazlewood to take the return catch on his left.
Wide! Just over the tramline. Josh Hazlewood serves it very full and outside off. Left alone.
Very full and on middle. Conway digs it to point for one more..
A single as this is hit to long on. 150 up for the Kiwis.
FOUR! That was hit hard! Short and outside off. Phillips opens his body up and smashes it over to long off for a boundary.

Big swing and a miss! Short of a length and outside off. Phillips clears his front leg as he looks to go big on the off side but misses. A stifled appeal follows but Australia are not quite convinced. Still, Aaron Finch takes the review. Ultra Edge shows no bat. Australia lose both the review.
Length and on top of middle. Conway pulls it to long on for a single.
A single to end! Not the best of nights for Zampa as he ends with figures of 4-0-39-1. On the pads, this is worked towards square leg for one.
Fuller and on middle, Conway somehow hits it past cover and takes two more.
FOUR! Thumped down the ground! A little too full and Conway makes Zampa pay. It is on off, this is smashed down the ground to the long off fence.
That is lovely bowling! Slows it up, lands it outside off and gets it to turn away a little. Devon Conway is beaten as he looks to go over covers.
WIDE! Fires this one down the leg side. Left alone. Wided.
Shorter and on off, this is pushed through covers for one.
Shorter and outside off, this is slapped through covers for one. The throw comes towards Zampa, he gets an awkward bounce and hence, does not stop it cleanly. No extra run taken.
A dot to end but another productive over for the Kiwis! On middle, defended.
Excellent running! This guy is really quick! Shorter and on middle, Glenn Phillips looks to pull, it goes off the top edge towards fine leg. Two taken.
FOUR! Magical timing! Fuller and on off, Glenn Phillips leans into it and strokes itwide of sweeper cover for a boundary. Beautifully timed.
Angled into the middle pole, blocked.
Good length and on off, defended.
Misfield and more runs! Fuller and on off, this is driven towards cover. The fielder there lets it through. Mid off gives it a chase and hurls it back. Three taken till then.
Glenn Phillips comes in.

A HUGE SHOUT AND THE FINGER IS RAISED! WILLIAMSON HAS BEEN GIVEN OUT LBW! He reviews right before the timer runs out. OUT! THREE REDS AND WILLIAMSON HAS TO WALK BACK! He takes a review along with him. That was not a good review to be honest. That just looked plumb if there was not bat. Zampa provides the breakthrough his side desperately needed. This is very full. Kane Williamson looks to play a shot which is probably not in his comfort zone. He tries the reverse sweep but this is quite full and on off. He misses to get hit on the pads. An appeal and the finger is raised. Timely wicket as they two were upping the ante.
That semed like it was in the slot! On middle, Conway gets the slog sweep out, it goes off the inner half through mid-wicket for one.
Outside off, shorter, this is cut through point for one more.
Shorter and outside off, this is slapped through covers for one.
Two! Really good batting! Steps out again but does not get to the pitch of it. Works it with soft hands towards long on and takes two.

SIX! Conway straightaway goes after Zampa and gets the full result. Steps out and does not quite get to the pitch of the ball but still goes ahead with the shot. He manages to clear the mid-wicket fence for a biggie. Pressure on Zampa who has been expensive so far.
End of a top over from Starc! Just the five singles from it. A yorker to end, Conway plays it towards cover and gets to the other end.
Really good from Starc! Another yorker on middle, all Williamson can do is jam it out towards mid-wicket and take one.
Full and on middle, Conway works it towards mid-wicket and takes one.
Well bowled! Williamson makes room and Starc follows him. He looks to flick but gets an inside edge onto the pads. The ball rolls on the off side. A run taken.
A yorker on off, Conway jams it down to third man and takes one.
Shorter and outside off, yet again it does not come onto the bat. Conway looks to cut but ends up chopping it to the keeper.
Another single to end! A decent comeback by Stoinis after going for a biggie earlier on but it is still a good over for the Kiwis. On the body, shorter, this is pulled through square leg for one.
Slightly shorter and on the pads, Conway pulls it down to fine leg for two.
A slower bumper this time, holds in the surface a touch. Williamson's one hand comes off the handle as he tries to pull, it goes towards deep square leg for one more.
Bangs it short, Conway pulls it nicely through square leg for one.
And again, you could see Williamson went hard there too. Full and outside off, Williamson looks to go over covers but it goes off the toe-end towards mid off for one.

SIX! What a shot that is! Lovely! Trademark Kane Williamson! This is angled into the pads, he plays the pick-up shot and it sails over the square leg fence. Intentions clear after the break. New Zealand probably will look to up the ante now.

Bangs a bouncer on middle. Conway pulls it to deep square leg for a brace. At the halfway mark, New Zealand are 97 for 1. Since the wicket of Finn Allen, the run rate has dropped down but not drastically. A lot of work to do for Australia now.

A stifled appeal for LBW but Mitchell Starc is not sure if it is pad first. No, clearly it was off the bat, a big inside edge. A corker of a yorker, around off. Conway digs it out off the inside edge and the ball bounces over the leg pole and goes to the keeper. Starc is not sure to review and so was not the keeper. Aaron Finch does not review. He did the good thing in the end.
On a length and outside off. Williamson punches it through point for one more.
A single as this is hit through point.
Two runs! A length ball, outside off. Conway punches it through covers and the batters get easy couple.
This is full and on middle. Williamson works it to deep mid-wicket for a single.

Not out it is! Adam Zampa appeals for LBW. He thinks it is pad first. Aaron Finch feels the same and takes the review. It does look like pad first in slow motion. Ultra Edge confirms the same. Ball Tracking shows wickets missing, the ball is going over the middle pole. Conway will continue. That was a good review nonetheless. A flatter ball on middle. Conway gets his pad across as he looks to defend but misses. Adam Zampa puts on a big appeal. The length was just short and the ball goes over. Australia lose the review.
SIX! BANG! Welcome boundary! The boundaries just dried up in the last over or so. Flighted, full and on middle. Conway comes down the track and launches it over long on for a biggie.
Tossed up, around off, slower in the air. Conway reverse sweeps it but finds short third man.
Another single as Williamson works it to long on.
Full and on leg. Conway flicks it to deep mid-wicket for one.
Tossed up, drifting on middle. Williamson forces it to long on for run.
Tad short and on middle, Kane pulls it to deep square leg for a single.
Wide! A bouncer at 130 clicks on middle. Williamson ducks. A wide given for height. Marcus Stoinis shakes his head.
A slower ball, length and angling on leg. Williamson is deceived as he pulls it back to the keeper.
On middle, flicked to mid-wicket for one more.
Length ball, outside off. Williamson punches off the back foot through covers for a single.
Australia have not been tight! Too many deliveries down the leg side. This is on the pads, Conway tucks it to deep square leg for a single.
Good running! Couple of runs! Length ball, around leg. Conway bunts it to mid-wicket and takes a brace.
A quicker ball on middle. Conway eases it to long on for a single.
A googly, no sharp turn. This is around off and Kane works it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Zampa bowls it on the pads, it's flicked through square leg for a single.
Zampa floats it full and outside off. Williamson uses his feet and drills it to long on for one.
On the pads, clipped to square leg for one.
FOUR! New Zealand are not allowing any bowlers to settle! Zampa gets the same treatment. This is full and outside off. Conway smashes it through covers for a boundary.
Tight from Cummins! So, a good couple of overs from Aussies but the damage was done before. This is on middle. Williamson defends it out. At the end of the Powerplay, New Zealand are 65 for 1.
On a length and on middle. Williamson nudges it to mid-wicket.
Outside off, guided to deep point for a single.
Length and on off, knocked to mid off.

FOUR! Not more as New Zealand hit a boundary! This is very full and outside off. Conway does well to guide it through point. The fielder in the deep runs to his right and dives to in vain. A boundary.
On middle, Conway plays it to mid-wicket.
Another dot to end! On middle, Williamson plays it to mid-wicket. End of a really good over from Josh Hazlewood, an over his side needed.
FOUR! Finds the gap! Lovely placement. Shorter and outside off, Williamson makes use of the little width that was on offer and guides it past point for a boundary. He is off the mark.
Williamson steps out, this is on middle, it is worked to mid-wicket. Four dots in the over so far.
Plays that well! Length again and on off, takes off after landing. Kane Williamson does well to guide it to point by getting on top of the bounce.
On a length and around off, kept out.
Kane Williamson is the new man in. Halt in play due to some technical issue. Not quite sure what.

OUT! TIMBER! Josh Hazlewood is absolutely thrilled and there is a look of relief on the Aussie players' face as they have gotten rid of Allen. That is a corker of a yorker from the best bowler of this format currently. Allen yet again steps down the track but this is very full, a yorker. Allen swings but this sneaks under the bat and hits the stumps. A top innings from Allen. Have to say, he has done his job. He usually has the role to get his side off to a flier and has done so. He though misses out on a well-deserved half ton. Can the Aussies build on this now?
Change. Josh Hazlewood is back on.

Had Stoinis stopped that, there could have been half a chance! Australia have been a tad sloppy so far in the field. On off, this is pushed to the left of Stoinis. Allen is off for a run. Stoinis fails to collect it cleanly and the single is easy in the end.

SIX! Fifty up for the Kiwis in no time! Another biggie for him and he is into the 40s in no time! Uses his feet again and makes this length ball into a full one, he hits it high up in the air but has the distance on this one too as it clears the long on fence.
Tip and run! On off, Conway pushes it towards cover and gets to the other end. Gets Allen on strike who is going great guns.
Two dots in a row! A slower one outside off, well outside off actually. Conway reaches out for it. It goes off the underedge to the keeper.
Halt! Saw dust has been poured near the bowler's landing area.
That really took off! Shorter and on the body, Conway looks to pull but this gets big on him. He is beaten. Half an appeal but turned down. Maxwell thought there is an edge but nothing from the rest.
Two more! Fuller and outside off, Conway strokes it through covers for a couple.
Change. Marcus Stoinis to have a go now.
Two to end another huge over! Fuller and on off, Allen pushes it through covers. The outfield is not that fast. Two taken.

SIX! Over the fence! Not sure about what length to bowl to Allen at the moment. Bowl full, he is hitting you down the ground and if you bowl short, he is pulling it in the stands. Shorter and on middle, this is pulled over the mid-wicket fence for a biggie.
A rare dot! Cummins goes for a yorker but ends up bowling a low full toss outside off, it is pushed to cover.
FOUR! All these runs will be hurting Zampa! Allen steps out again, Cummins bowls it on a length. Allen hits it over mid off and this races away to the fence again. Raining boundaries here.

DROPPED AND FOUR! That has bursts through the hands of Zampa! Shorter and slower but down the leg side. Allen is through the shot as he tries to pull. It goes more off the toe-end towards short fine leg. Zampa looks to take it above his head but it goes through and down to the fence. He should have taken that and Australia needed it to be caught. This could prove very costly as Allen is in the mood here.
Yet again, a single, these singles will just not let the pressure build! This is fuller and on off, Conway looks to drive, it goes off the inner half through square leg for one.
Starc, Hazlewood and now time for Pat Cummins.

FOUR! That has been crunched! It went to the fence like a tracer bullet. Cracking sound of the bat too and that boundary means 15 came from the second over. Allen makes room and steps out, this is on a length and around off. It is hammered through covers and it races away to the fence.

Brilliant! No dots in this over so far. If not a boundary, a single. Josh Hazlewood comes around the wicket and bowls it on a length and on off, Conway plays it late and on the off side for a quick run.

FOUR! Class, this guy is full of class! Another top shot. Conway steps out, he does not get to the length of the ball as Josh Hazlewood drags it back. Conway still manages to stroke it on the up, gets on top of the bounce and hits it past mid off for another boundary.
Slightly shorter, Allen looks to pull, this goes more off the inside half through mid-wicket for one.
Tip and run! Superb stuff from Devon Conway! Josh Hazlewood gets it right, he bowls it on a length and around off, Conway drops it towards cover for one.
Halt in play. Josh Hazlewood pulls out in the last moment as Conway gets distracted by a man walking near the sight screen.

FOUR! Tickled nice and fine! Conway is underway with a boundary too. This is not the start Finch or Australia would have wanted. This is so not Josh Hazlewood! He starts off with one on the pads. It is worked down to fine leg for another boundary. Dealing in boundaries at the moment are the Kiwis.
Who will bowl from the other end? It is Josh Hazlewood. A slip and fine third man in place for Conway.

A dot to end but that is the most expensive first over by an Australian bowler in T20Is. Starc bangs it in, tennis-ball like bounce on this delivery. Allen is through the pull and gets beaten. 14 from the first over. An electrifying start to the game here.

FOUR! Down the ground! Allen is on a mission here. Yet again a delivery in his slot. It is full and on off, Allen slams it down the ground, this time it is as straight as an arrow and it reaches the fence.
Change of pace! Starc goes full, a slower one though and it is almost a yorker outside off. It is jammed towards mid off.

SIX! This is even better! Absolutely brilliant. He has treated Starc with disdain here. Fuller again, Starc is not learning, there is no swing but he continues to look for it. In the process, he is bowling slot balls. Allen thumps it over the long on fence and it goes for a biggie. First of the game. New Zealand off to a flier.

FOUR! What a shot that is! Wow! That is some confidence. Yes, it is a half volley, yes, it is right in the slot for Allen but in such a big game, pulling that shot out on the second ball itself shows how fearless this guy is. He tonks it over the mid on fielder and bags a boundary to get off the mark.
Starc goes full, in search of some swing. He tries to get it back in from outside off but not a lot of movement. Allen strokes it to mid on.

All set now. Gear up everyone, to kick off the mega event. The Aussies are out in the middle. Devon Conway and Finn Allen are the openers for the Kiwis. Mitchell Starc to start with the new ball. A slip in place. Here we go...

We are all set for the action. So far so good with the weather. Let's hope it stays away. The players walk out along with the two umpires. As we see every time before the game starts, it will be time for the national anthems. New Zealand's first followed by Australia's.
NEW ZEALAND (Playing XI) - Devon Conway, Finn Allen, Kane Williamson (C), Glenn Phillips (WK), Mark Chapman, James Neesham, Mitchell Santner, Ish Sodhi, Tim Southee, Lockie Ferguson, Trent Boult.
AUSTRALIA (Playing XI) - David Warner, Aaron Finch (C), Mitchell Marsh, Glenn Maxwell, Marcus Stoinis, Tim David, Matthew Wade (WK), Mitchell Starc, Pat Cummins, Adam Zampa, Josh Hazlewood.

Kane Williamson, the captain of New Zealand says they wanted to bowl first too but they'll make good use of the wicket now. Adds it is now about focusing on this game and not think about the plans and try and execute the plans. Informs about his team.

Aaron Finch, the captain of Australia says there is weather around and he feels the wicket gets better. States every time one plays for the Aussies there is pressure and everyone wants to do well. Informs Steven Smith, Cameron Green, Kane Richardson and Ashton Agar are not playing.
TOSS - AUSTRALIA have won the toss and they will BOWL first!

PITCH REPORT - Simon Doull says the wicket looks really good. Isha Guha then says it is a slow kind of a wicket and there is something in it for both, the pacers and the spinners. Adds it though has been under cover and the skipper might be tempted to bowl first after winning the toss. Informs the average score is around 160.

Enough about the teams now, let us talk about the weather, the forecast is not that great and there are dark clouds above but the rain has stayed away for now and let us hope it remains that way and we get a full game of cricket.

For New Zealand, Australia is not a place they enjoying visiting. Also, the hosts are not an opponent they fancy playing. They have won, just the one game in the last 17 against the Aussies in Australia. To add to that, they have not been in the best of forms heading into this World Cup. They were recently beaten by Pakistan in their own country. However, just like their opponents, they too are a side who have been doing unexpectedly well when it matters. Despite the form, the Kiwis are not a side one can discard.

The Aussies are yet again heavy favourites in the tournament. They are the defending champions and with the tournament being played in their own backyard, you have to term them as favourites to go all the way. However, no side yet has been able to defend the title. Also, the Aussies, in recent times have not been in the best of forms in this format. They head into this tournament after being beaten by England quite comprehensively. The hosts though are a side who thrive when it matters the most. The look of their side is more or less similar to what they had in the last World Cup and Finch will be eager to start off with a win.

IT IS TIME! It is time for the mega event! The first game of the T20I World Cup and it is a clash between the two finalists of the last editions, the Trans-Tasmain rivals will lock horns to kick things off. It is Australia taking on New Zealand at the SCG. This promises to be an absolute cracker. Stay tuned.
... MATCH DAY ...
